sources.title: Indian Contract Act, 1872
sources.note: The official indexed excerpt supplies the capacity provision; direct PDF retrieval timed out. An adult-account proposal requires a product age-policy decision, not merely revised text.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
sources.note: Read with the commencement notification. Publication of the Act is not commencement of every obligation.

sources.title: G.S.R. 843(E), DPDP commencement notification
sources.note: Provides immediate, one-year and eighteen-month commencement phases from Gazette publication.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, G.S.R. 846(E)
sources.note: Commencement varies by rule. Do not describe every duty as already operational on the review date.

sources.title: Information Technology (Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 2011
sources.locator: G.S.R. 313(E), rules 4-8 in the Gazette compilation
sources.note: SPDI notification retrieved from a Government of India mirror; the compilation also contains other 2011 rules. Only the identified SPDI notification is relied on, not repealed intermediary provisions.

sources.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
sources.note: Official PDF retrieved and hashed. The 48-hour acknowledgement and one-month redress duties already exist where the rules apply; they are not optional proposed future standards.

sources.title: Government announcement explaining the 2026 e-commerce amendments
sources.locator: 10 September 2026 release; commencement and key amendments
sources.note: Official release gives 1 January 2027 commencement and describes complaint copies, NCH convergence and transparency. The full amendment Gazette still needs clause-level verification.

sources.title: CERT-In directions under section 70B, 28 April 2022
sources.note: Covered entities: report listed incidents within six hours; retain ICT logs 180 days within India. This is not a universal retention period for every ride record.

sources.title: Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025
sources.note: A central framework does not resolve the operative requirements in each pickup jurisdiction.

sources.title: UP March 2026 transport consultation draft
sources.note: Consultation draft. Never use as proof of a final operative penalty, exemption or service condition. Final-rule reconciliation remains open.

sources.title: Delhi 2023 transport scheme, official publication page
sources.note: Owner confirms Delhi pickups. The scheme has its own at-least-25-vehicle scope clause; it does not waive other applicable law. Fleet counting and current amendments need territory-specific verification.

sources.title: Haryana transport notification, 21 May 2026
sources.note: Full attachment retrieval timed out. Haryana is a research candidate only; do not assert scope, thresholds or compliance from the index.

sources.title: UP Motor Vehicles (Thirty-third Amendment) rules, notification 5/2026/470 of 22 May 2026
sources.note: Final order retrieved from the current transport portal, including completed consultation recitals. Replaces the earlier draft as the audit authority; no automatic conclusion about implementation or exemptions.

sources.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 789(E)
sources.note: Full Gazette retrieved and visual commencement checked; adds complaint-copy and NCH convergence duties and other transparency changes. Existing 2020 grievance timing is not postponed to 2027.

sources.title: Rajasthan Motor Vehicles Aggregator Scheme Rules, 2025
sources.note: Owner confirms Rajasthan pickups. Applicability clause has at least 25 associated vehicles; eligibility wording differs from UP. No blanket exemption conclusion.

sources.title: Punjab Vehicles Aggregator draft rules, 14 December 2023
sources.locator: Official notification index expressly calls it draft
sources.note: A final current state text was not established. Do not treat the draft as operative law or interpret an unresolved state framework as permission to disregard central law.
